_comment: The MoE thesis, as a ceiling computation. docs/MINING.md's first open surface is 'a model with less weight traffic per token', because the persist ceiling is 2*min(capacity,footprint)/step_traffic and the numerator is pinned at 60 MiB by the cache. Qwen3.8-27B is a DENSE hybrid moving 18.5 GB per batch-1 step, which is why that ceiling is 0.68%. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is the same architecture family - Gated DeltaNet + full attention, the same runtime, the same hook - with a sparse MoE FFN: 256 experts, 8 used per token. eval/traffic_budget.py --matrix reads this. Arms are control-arm measurements on ONE box; the geometry is read from the checkpoint, not assumed.
_persisting_l2_bytes_note: persisting_l2_max_bytes as queried by tools/info.cpp: 60 MiB of a 96 MiB L2. Unchanged by the model - this is the numerator the whole thesis is about, and it is fixed by the device.

model.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, unsloth UD-Q4_K_M GGUF, 22.1 GB
model._geometry_source: read from the GGUF's own metadata and tensor shapes, not from the runtime's defaults: block_count 40, full_attention_interval 4 (so 30 recurrent layers, confirmed by which blocks carry ssm_* tensors), ssm.state_size 128, ssm.group_count 16 (linear_q_heads), blk.0.attn_qkv.weight [2048, 8192] so linear_qkvdim 8192 and linear_v_heads (8192 - 2*16*128)/128 = 32, ssm.conv_kernel 4.
model._state_formulas: lin_state = linear_v_heads * linear_head_dim^2 * sizeof(float) (qwen35.cpp:560); lin_conv = (linear_conv_kernel-1) * linear_qkvdim * sizeof(bf16) (qwen35.cpp:559). Both formulas reproduce the pinned Qwen3.8-27B numbers exactly.

_active_weight_bytes_note: Weight bytes one decode step reads, summed from the checkpoint's own tensor table and quantisation types: 1.5975 GB of per-block non-expert weights (attn_qkv Q8_0, attn_gate, ssm_out, the shared expert, the router), 0.4172 GB of output head (Q6_K), and 0.6115 GB for the 8 of 256 experts a token routes to. token_embd is excluded - one row per token. traffic_budget.py adds the recurrent-state traffic it computes and reports the ratio against measured-time x peak bandwidth, which says whether the ceiling above is tight or merely true. Note this assumes every row in a concurrent batch routes to the same experts, which is exactly what qwen3_gguf_cb_bench does - it submits one identical prompt per request. A production batch of DIFFERENT prompts would touch far more of the 256 experts per step, raising the denominator and lowering the recurrent share.
